title: Modelling Dissolved Oxygen Profiles in Cascade Aerators for Groundwater Pre-Treatment: Field Validation at Three Sites in Vojvodina

record.title: Modelling Dissolved Oxygen Profiles in Cascade Aerators for Groundwater Pre-Treatment: Field Validation at Three Sites in Vojvodina
record.abstract: A one-dimensional plug-flow mass-transfer model for dissolved oxygen (DO) re-aeration in multi-step cascade aerators was calibrated and validated against field measurements at three groundwater treatment stations in Vojvodina. Model inputs included weir geometry, step height (0.15–0.35 m), number of steps (4–8), and inlet DO (0.1–1.8 mg/L). The overall volumetric mass-transfer coefficient KLa ranged from 0.12 to 0.41 min⁻¹ across sites; a correlation with hydraulic loading rate (r² = 0.87) was derived. Outlet DO predictions deviated from measured values by less than 8% at all three sites across twelve sampling campaigns. The calibrated model was used to evaluate retrofitting options for an ageing four-step cascade needing to achieve DO > 7 mg/L for downstream biological Mn oxidation. Sensitivity analysis identified step height and flow per unit weir width as the dominant design variables.
